claims.claim: People who cannot walk may be eligible for a Blue Badge.
claims.note: The guidance lists being unable to walk at all among the grounds for possibly getting a badge.

claims.claim: People who have severe difficulty walking may be eligible for a Blue Badge.
claims.quote: you find walking very difficult due to pain, breathlessness or the time it takes
claims.note: The guidance lists finding walking very difficult among the grounds for possibly getting a badge.

claims.claim: People registered severely sight impaired are eligible for a Blue Badge.
claims.quote: you are registered blind (severely sight impaired)
claims.note: Being registered blind (severely sight impaired) gives automatic qualification.

claims.claim: People with a hidden disability causing very considerable difficulty may be eligible for a Blue Badge.
claims.quote: If you have a non-visible (hidden) condition, you will also be asked questions around how journeys between your vehicle and destination are affected by your condition.
claims.note: The text covers applicants with hidden conditions, but does not state a 'very considerable difficulty' test for them; it lists specific journey-related criteria instead.

claims.claim: Receiving the enhanced rate of the PIP mobility component qualifies you for a Blue Badge.
claims.quote: you receive a Personal Independence Payment ( PIP ) because you can’t walk more than 50 metres (a score of 8 points or more under the ‘moving around’ activity of the mobility component)
claims.note: The text ties automatic qualification to specific PIP mobility scores (8+ points for moving around, or 10 points under descriptor E), not to the enhanced rate as such.

claims.claim: The PIP mobility award must be confirmed with proof.
claims.quote: You’ll also be asked to provide proof of the PIP award.
claims.note: Applicants are asked to provide proof of the PIP award, including the mobility scores page of the DWP letter.
